# Nomo — Live Activity on your iPhone

                 

Nomo mirrors your **Claude Code**, **OpenAI Codex** (CLI and desktop app), **OpenCode**, **Cursor**, **Antigravity** and **Devin** sessions to the Nomo iPhone app as a Live Activity — working, needs you, done — and lets you answer permission prompts and questions from the phone. Everything is end-to-end encrypted; one pairing covers every agent on a computer. This README is the **technical and security reference**. How to install, pair, use the commands, update and uninstall lives at **[docs.nomo.gg](https://docs.nomo.gg)**. > [!NOTE] > Developed and tested on **macOS** and **Linux**. **Windows is untested** (the hooks are pure Node > built-ins, but nothing has been verified there), so treat it as unsupported. ## Security at a glance - **End-to-end encrypted.** Every session update is sealed with **AES-256-GCM** on your computer and opened only on your iPhone. The key comes from pairing (QR secret or six-word code, then a per-pairing ephemeral **ECDH P-256** exchange) and never passes through a server. [Encryption](#encryption) - **The relay is blind.** The Cloudflare Worker that forwards pushes sees routing metadata only — never a title, machine name, status text, command or answer. The one thing it sees in the clear is the presence ping (once a minute, and when it changes): which agents have a turn open, and whether one is waiting for approval. A free (not Pro) pairing sends only that ping and the sealed daily activity summary, except that after a quiet spell the first prompt's requests still go out (end-to-end encrypted, as always) and are refused. [What leaves your computer](#what-leaves-your-computer) - **No telemetry, no credentials.** The plugin's only network peer is that relay (`https://api.nomo.gg` by default). It never reads your agents' API keys or logins, and has no analytics. The installer and `/nomo-update` also run `git` against `github.com/KarrixLee/nomo`. [Network](#network) - **Hooks can only do what you answered.** A phone Allow, Deny or answer is acted on only when it is sealed by your paired phone for that exact request. Every failure — unpaired, offline, timeout, crash — **fails open** to the agent's own prompt. Nomo can delay a decision; it never makes one for you, except auto-approving its **own** status commands, matched byte for byte. Nomo's own pair, unpair, reset and uninstall commands always ask. [Hooks security](#hooks-security) - **Phone commands are sealed and narrow.** Interrupt, Reply (Antigravity, OpenCode 2.x) and Open on Mac run only when sealed by your paired phone, fresh (under 2 minutes) and never replayed, for a session this computer tracks. A reply is handed to the agent as a user message; nothing from the phone is ever run as a shell command. [OpenCode 2.x remote control](#opencode-plugin) - **Local files are owner-only.** Pairing keys and session records live in `~/.config/cc-status/`, written `0600`. Every file Nomo writes into an agent's config is listed below, and the installers merge rather than overwrite. [Files on your computer](#files-on-your-computer) - **Unpair revokes the pairing on the server** and deletes the local keys (even when the server is unreachable); uninstall removes only Nomo's own entries. Steps: [docs.nomo.gg/sessions/commands](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/commands). - **Open source (MIT), zero npm dependencies.** The bundles in `plugin/dist/` are what runs, committed and reproducible from `src/`. [Development](#development) ## Install ```sh bunx nomo-ai # or: npx nomo-ai ``` It detects which agents are on this computer, opens a picker with those agents already ticked, and on Enter installs Nomo for each through that agent's own install path (`--claude` `--codex` `--opencode` `--cursor` `--antigravity` `--devin` pick agents; `-n` prints the plan and runs nothing). There is no `postinstall` hook. **Pairing stays an explicit yes.** In an interactive terminal (stdin and stdout both a TTY), once at least one agent is installed and this computer is not already paired, the installer asks `Pair your phone now? [Y/n]`; yes runs exactly `nomo pair`. It never pairs without that answer: `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `CI=…` and piped or scripted runs never ask and never pair, and a computer that is already paired is never re-paired (re-pairing revokes the old pairing). Pair any time with `nomo pair` or the pair command inside your agent. Pairing before restarting the agents is fine for all of them, and OpenCode needs it that way round: it reads the pairing once, at start. Devin can instead use the plugin: `devin plugins install KarrixLee/nomo`. The three agent config files it merges into directly are undone with `nomo uninstall --cursor`, `nomo uninstall --antigravity` and `nomo uninstall --devin` (also spelled `--uninstall`; the same as `node ~/.nomo/plugin/scripts/-install.mjs --uninstall`). `nomo uninstall --opencode` deletes the plugin stub and the `/nomo-*` command files `opencode-install.sh` wrote (only files carrying its marker; your other plugins, commands and `opencode.json` are untouched), then asks you to restart OpenCode (`opencode service restart` for the 2.x background service). `--dry-run` lists what it would remove. An agent flag is required. For Claude Code and Codex, uninstall only prints the host's own removal command. **Commands**, from any folder, for any agent: ```sh nomo pair # pair with your phone (QR page, then waits for the scan); `pair code` for the typeable code nomo status # is this computer paired, and is each agent set up nomo reset # clear stuck sessions and send your activity summary now nomo unpair # disconnect this computer from your phone (every agent on it) nomo uninstall --cursor # remove Nomo from an agent you name ``` They run the same plugin code as the in-agent commands (`/nomo-cc:pair`, `$nomo-reset`, `/nomo-status`, …), and pairing, sessions and the watchdog are shared by every agent on a computer, so one `reset` or `pair` here covers all of them. **Short `nomo` command.** The installer also adds a short `nomo` command (`bun add -g nomo-ai`, or `npm install -g nomo-ai` when not run from bun; no `sudo`), so `nomo pair`, `nomo status`, … work from any folder; pass `--no-global` to skip it, and remove it with `bun remove -g nomo-ai` (or `npm uninstall -g nomo-ai`). Without it, every command works the same as `bunx nomo-ai pair`, `bunx nomo-ai status`, … (`npx nomo-ai …` when you ran the installer with npx; its hints name that form) Never type `bunx nomo` or `npx nomo`: the npm package named `nomo` is someone else's. The full guides live at [docs.nomo.gg](https://docs.nomo.gg): | | | | --- | --- | | **Get started** | [Install](https://docs.nomo.gg/setup/install) · [Pair your iPhone](https://docs.nomo.gg/setup/pairing) | | **Everyday use** | [Answer from your phone](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/approvals) · [Commands, update and uninstall](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/commands) | | **Each agent** | [Codex](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/codex) · [OpenCode](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/opencode) · [Cursor](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/cursor) · [Antigravity](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/antigravity) · [Devin](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/devin) | | **Help** | [Troubleshooting](https://docs.nomo.gg/sessions/troubleshooting) | ## Architecture Pairing establishes **one shared key** that only your phone and computer hold. It can be handed over two ways, both keeping it off every server: - **Scan the QR** on the local pairing page. The QR carries a random pairing secret that exists only in the code image; the phone mixes it with its own nonce (HKDF-SHA256). - **Type the one-time code** — six words and a channel number (e.g. `7-ocean-sunset-mango-river-atlas-cabin`). The phone runs PBKDF2-SHA256 over the words to rebuild the same secret, then the same HKDF step. The words never leave the pairing page; the channel is a one-time routing handle that burns on first use and expires in 10 minutes. The plugin seals every update before it leaves the machine; the relay Worker and Apple's push service carry ciphertext only, and the iPhone decrypts (for the Live Activity, in the widget at render time). Diagram source: [`assets/architecture.excalidraw`](assets/architecture.excalidraw) — open it at [excalidraw.com](https://excalidraw.com) to edit. ### The pairing code is never printed By default the one-time code is shown **only on the pairing page** (a local `file://` page, `0600`, with no fonts, remote images, analytics or CDN), behind "Tap to reveal code". It is never printed to the terminal, so it cannot land in shell history, a screen recording or an AI transcript. `pair.mjs --show-code` (the `pair code` form of each agent's pair command) is the deliberate opt-out for a headless or SSH-only box: it prints the code to stdout, where it is sensitive for the ~10 minutes it is valid. The page is deleted when pairing completes. ## Encryption - **AES-256-GCM** seals every session update, approval card and answer. The relay can route by pairing id but cannot read a field. - **Six BIP39 words (~66 bits)**, stretched with **PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations** (salted with the pairing id), put an offline brute-force of the code — what a logging relay could try against the known-plaintext pairing blob — out of reach. - **Forward secrecy via a per-pairing ephemeral ECDH (P-256) ratchet.** The QR secret or code only bootstraps a handshake key. Computer and phone each generate a throwaway keypair, do an ECDH, and mix the result with the bootstrap key into the key that encrypts your sessions; the throwaway private keys are discarded after pairing. A code leaked **after** pairing cannot decrypt anything, and mixing it into the handshake means a relay that swaps the public keys (man-in-the-middle) makes pairing fail rather than succeed under its key. Only public keys transit the relay in the clear. - **Each sealed update names its own session.** The session id travels in the clear for routing, so the sealed blob repeats it (`sid`). The app treats a blob whose sealed `sid` differs from the session it is listed under as unreadable, so a relay cannot relabel one session's update as another's and steer an approval or interrupt onto the wrong session. (Plugins older than this send no `sid`; their updates are still shown.) - **LAN fast path has its own seal.** Local-network traffic is sealed under `K_lan` = HKDF-SHA256(pairing key, info `nomo-lan-v1|`), so nobody on the Wi-Fi can read even the metadata, and a relay ciphertext will not open on the LAN channel (or vice versa). See [LAN fast path](#lan-fast-path). ## What leaves your computer ### Network | Destination | When | What | |---|---|---| | Relay Worker (`https://api.nomo.gg`, or `NOMO_WORKER_URL` at pair time) | every session event; approval holds; pairing; unpair; the activity summary; presence about once a minute while an agent session is open, plus one when it changes (at most every ~27 s) | `/v1/cc/event`, `/v1/cc/decision*`, `/v1/cc/full`, `/v1/cc/pair/*`, `/v1/cc/presence` | | Your iPhone, on the same network (only if LAN is turned on in the app) | commands and answers | `POST /v1/lan`, sealed under `K_lan` | | `github.com/KarrixLee/nomo` via `git` | `bunx nomo-ai` (OpenCode, Cursor, Antigravity, Devin legs) and `/nomo-update` | clone / fetch / pull of this repo | | The npm registry, via your package manager | `bunx nomo-ai`, for the short `nomo` command (skip with `--no-global`) | `bun add -g nomo-ai` or `npm install -g nomo-ai` | Nothing else: no analytics, no crash reporting, no reads of agent credentials. **In the clear to the relay** (needed to route and authenticate): the pairing id and the computer's pairing secret (headers), the plugin version, whether remote approvals are on, and per event the session id, the op (`start` / `update` / `done` / `end`), a priority, timestamps, and — for a Codex `request_user_input` question only — `attentionKind: "userInput"`. **Sealed**: everything else — title, machine name, folder, status, model, tool name, command, file path, plan text, questions, answers, and which agent produced the event. The diff on an edit approval (patch or edit content, line counts) is sealed the same way as a command, in the card and in a full-text pull. For an overwrite (a whole-file write onto an existing file) the plugin reads that file from disk — a regular UTF-8 text file up to 2 MiB, never a device, FIFO or directory — so the diff also carries the current file's changed lines. **Daily activity summary — counts only, sealed.** While paired, the watchdog reads your agents' local history read-only — Claude Code transcripts (`~/.claude/projects`), Codex rollouts and its `state_5.sqlite` / `thread_history_1.sqlite`, OpenCode's `opencode.db` — and builds one row per day per agent: session count, prompt count, which 5-minute slots had activity, and token totals per model. It **never** puts prompt or reply text, project names or paths into the summary. Rows are kept in `~/.config/cc-status/activity-days.json` (at most 400 days) and, at most every 6 hours and only when changed, sealed and uploaded to `/v1/cc/full` (`what: "activity"`); right after pairing a new phone the existing rows go up once within about a minute, and after a plugin update new rows go up at the next scan instead of waiting the 6 hours. To send it right away, run `nomo reset` (or reset inside your agent: `/nomo-cc:reset`, `$nomo-reset`, `/nomo-reset`): it scans and uploads once, then says whether it was sent. The relay cannot read them and deletes them after **35 days**. The summary carries a random per-computer id (`mid`) so the phone does not count a computer twice — a UUID made once and kept in `~/.config/cc-status/machine-id` (owner-only), **never** derived from serial, MAC, hostname or user name; delete the file for a new one. **Presence — two fields, every pairing.** About once a minute while the watchdog runs (an agent session is open), and as soon as the answer changes (never more than once per ~27 s), the plugin POSTs `/v1/cc/presence` with `{ "coding": [agent ids], "waiting": true|false }` plus one `"agent"` + `"pluginVersion"` pair (each agent's own Nomo integration version, one agent per POST in turn; left off against a relay that does not take them yet): which agents (`claude`, `codex`, …) have a turn open, and whether any session is waiting for an approval. No session id, title, folder, command or text. It is not sealed (the relay keeps it about 3 minutes so the phone can show "Claude is coding"), and the reply tells the plugin whether the pairing is Pro. **Free pairing (not Pro) — only presence and the activity summary leave the computer.** When the relay says a pairing is not Pro (the presence reply, or a 403 `{"error":"entitlement suspended"}` on any session route — or, from a relay that says so, the claim itself at pairing time), the plugin writes `~/.config/cc-status/free-mode` (removed on unpair, re-pair and a revoke teardown) and, while it is fresh (15 minutes, refreshed by each presence reply), sends **no** session events, opens **no** approval holds (every prompt goes straight to the agent's own dialog), uploads **no** plan or permission text, and keys the LAN listener off. Sessions are still tracked on disk so presence stays accurate. After a quiet spell (15 minutes with no presence reply) the marker has expired, so the first prompt's sealed requests go out (one event; on a permission prompt also the full text and the approval request), the relay refuses them and stores nothing, and free mode resumes. The LAN listener does not come back when the marker expires: it stays keyed off until the relay says the pairing is Pro (a presence reply, or an accepted session request), which deletes the marker. A 403 is never treated as an unpair (only a 404/410 is), and neither is a `409` (a pairing the relay has not seen claimed yet): a session event is retried later, and a prompt's approval request falls open to the agent's own prompt, as on any other relay error. **On the iPhone,** the Live Agents widget (Nomo Pro) reads a snapshot of decrypted titles, states and computer names from the app's own App Group container. It never leaves the device. ### Files on your computer | Path | What | Written by | |---|---|---| | `~/.config/cc-status/config.json` (`0600`) | pairing id, computer secret, 32-byte key; deleted by unpair (after a server revoke) | pair | | `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/*.json` (`0600`) | one record per live session (agent pid, last sealed blob) | hooks, watchdog | | `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/.devin-allow` (owner-only) | Devin "Always allow (this session)" grants; deleted by unpair, reset and pairing again | Devin approval hook | | `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/..agy-inbox` (owner-only) | queued Antigravity and OpenCode 2.x phone replies, deleted after a day | watchdog | | `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/.oc-interrupt` (owner-only) | an OpenCode 2.x Interrupt waiting for the plugin (consumed within ~1 s; ignored after 2 minutes) | watchdog | | `~/.config/cc-status/hook-shim.sh` (`0700`) | version-stable hook launcher | `run.sh`, pair | | `~/.config/cc-status/activity-days.json`, `machine-id` | activity summary, per-computer id | watchdog | | `~/.config/cc-status/free-mode` | time the relay last said this pairing is not Pro (counts for 15 minutes for sending; keeps the LAN listener off until the relay says Pro) | hooks, watchdog | | `~/.config/cc-status/short-command` | `1` or `0`: whether the short `nomo` command is installed, so status and reset name `nomo …` or `bunx nomo-ai …` | `bunx nomo-ai` | | `~/.config/cc-status/*-trace.log` (`0600`) | local diagnostics; never uploaded | hooks, watchdog | | `~/.codex/config.toml` | Codex `notify` backstop (your existing `notify` is chained, mode kept, one-time `config.toml.bak-nomo`); refuses an unparseable `notify` line | Codex pair; `nomo pair` (and the installer's pair question) when Codex has Nomo | | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/nomo.js`, `commands/nomo-*.md` | OpenCode stub + commands | `opencode-install.sh` | | `~/.cursor/hooks.json` (merged), `~/.cursor/skills/nomo-*/` | Cursor hooks + skills (`$CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` if set) | `cursor-install.mjs` | | `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (`"nomo"` block), `~/.gemini/config/plugins/nomo/` | Antigravity hooks + plugin | `antigravity-install.mjs` | | `~/.config/devin/config.json` (`"hooks"` key, merged), `~/.config/devin/skills/nomo-*/` | Devin hooks + skills | `devin-install.mjs` | | `~/.nomo/` | git checkout of this repo (OpenCode, Cursor, Antigravity, Devin installer) | `bunx nomo-ai` | Claude Code and Codex install through their own marketplaces; Nomo writes nothing into `~/.claude` or `~/.codex` except the Codex `notify` line above. `NOMO_CC_DIR` (testing only) moves the state folder; real installs never set it, and anything that can set your agent's environment could already change `HOME`. ## Hooks security ### Approval holds (all agents) - **Only sessions your phone is showing are answerable.** The hook holds the agent's prompt while the phone shows the card; the answer rides back sealed, so the relay never learns what you chose. - **Fail-open.** A network error, timeout or unpaired state before the hold is granted drops straight to the agent's own dialog. Once granted, a failed poll counts as a miss; ~5 minutes of consecutive misses gives up the same way. While the relay is reachable the hold has no ceiling of its own — it waits until you answer, the request expires or is superseded server-side, or the hook is killed (Esc at the terminal, or the agent's hook timeout). - **Approvals switch.** One machine-wide flag pauses remote approvals for every agent; prompts then go straight to the computer. - **Free pairings never hold.** While the pairing is not Pro (see [What leaves your computer](#what-leaves-your-computer)) every prompt goes straight to the agent's own dialog, exactly like the paused switch, and nothing is posted. - **Shell cards keep the command.** The model-written one-line description is a caption: shortened first, and dropped before the command when space runs out. - **The "Always allow" label is display-only.** At hold time the plugin seals what an Always-allow tap would grant into the card as `permissionGrant`: structured data, never prose, so the phone builds the label in its own language. Format: `""`, or one or more entries joined by `\n`, each `kind` or `kind:literal` (the literal is everything after the first `:`, has no control characters, is capped at 80 characters, and the phone shows it verbatim in monospace, never as Markdown). Kinds: `cmd:` (commands starting with it, or a Claude Code rule with a `*` wildcard shown as written), `exact` (this exact command), `domain:`, `edit:`, `dir:` (one folder), `dirs:` (N folders), `edits`, `reads`, `fetches`, `searches`, `commands` (every one of that kind), `planmode`, `automode`, `plans` (plan approvals), `tool:` (the whole tool) and `similar` (a rule the plugin can't name; also how the phone shows a kind it doesn't know). Any unnamed part, or a value over 240 characters, collapses to `similar`, never a shorter list. It is built from the same input as the answer: Claude Code's own suggestions (after the filter below), OpenCode's `always` patterns, or Devin's Nomo-side grant rule. `""` means the tap would only be a one-time allow, and the phone hides the option; absent (Codex, Antigravity, questions, older plugins) means unknown. It only labels the button: the rule itself is still decided and enforced by the agent. - **Claude Code Computer Use** app-access dialogs fire no answerable hook, so the phone shows a sealed heads-up naming the apps with no Allow/Deny; approve it on the computer. ### Claude Code hooks - Wired by the plugin's `hooks.json` (no `settings.json` edits). Status hooks are silent: unpaired → no-op; relay down → 2 s POST timeout, exit 0. They cannot affect the session. - `PermissionRequest` (timeout 24 h) is the only hook that answers. **"Always allow (this session)" stays in this session:** Claude Code often marks its suggested rules (e.g. `Bash(bun test:*)`) to be saved to `.claude/settings.local.json`; Nomo keeps the allow rules, extra directories and mode switches it suggested, rewrites every one to `destination: "session"`, and drops deny rules and the `bypassPermissions` / `dontAsk` modes. A phone tap never writes a settings file and the grant ends with the session. It never widens the suggestion: the whole-tool rule (e.g. plain `Read`) is used only when nothing was suggested; if everything suggested was dropped, the tap is a one-time allow. - Inside Devin (which also runs `~/.claude` hooks), Nomo's Claude Code hooks stand down, so a Devin session is never a Claude Code row and never answered by them. ### Codex hooks - The ten hooks ship in `plugin/hooks/codex-hooks.json` and stay **inert until you trust them** in Codex's `/hooks` review — Codex's own gate, which Nomo cannot pre-approve. The command lines are byte-stable across releases, so a trust holds through updates. - `PermissionRequest` (timeout 1 h) is the answering hook; status hooks are fail-silent like Claude Code's. Pairing also chains a `notify` backstop into `~/.codex/config.toml` (see [Files](#files-on-your-computer)). ### OpenCode plugin - One resident module inside OpenCode's server process; it must never throw, block, print or install process-wide signal handlers. One file serves OpenCode 1.x (`server`) and 2.x (`setup`). - **OpenCode 1.x:** it answers `permission.asked` (Allow / Always / Deny) and `question.asked`. **Always** is OpenCode's own `always` reply: it allows the request's `always` patterns (e.g. `git status *`, or `*` for every edit) for that project **until OpenCode restarts**, across its sessions — OpenCode keeps the rule in memory, never on disk. - **OpenCode 2.x:** it answers permissions through OpenCode's in-process `ctx.permission.reply`: Allow, **Always allow (saved for this project)**, Deny and **Deny with note**. 2.x saves an Always rule (the request's `save` patterns, e.g. `git status *`) to the project **on disk**, where it outlives restarts, so the card states it as `permissionProjectGrant` and only a phone that labels it "saved for this project" (app 2.5.3+) offers it; `permissionGrant` stays `""`, so an older app, whose OpenCode label says "until OpenCode restarts", keeps hiding Always. A note rides on the reject as OpenCode's `message`: the model reads it and keeps working (a plain Deny ends the step). A Deny rejects that request and every other one OpenCode raised in the same step (the same assistant message). Questions are 2.x forms, which plugins have no way to answer: the phone shows the session as waiting and you answer on the computer. - **OpenCode 2.x remote control — Reply and Interrupt.** These are new powers for your phone: **Reply** types a message into a session (as if you typed it in OpenCode), and **Interrupt** stops its running turn. Both arrive only as commands sealed by your paired phone and pass the watchdog's usual gates (decrypted under the pairing key, a kind on the allow-list, sealed less than 2 minutes ago, nonce never seen before, naming a session this computer tracks). The watchdog then leaves them as owner-only files in `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/`: a reply as one `.agy-inbox` file (at most 4,000 characters, no control characters but line breaks), an interrupt as `.oc-interrupt`. The plugin, inside OpenCode, checks once a second, acts only for sessions in its own folder, claims each file with an atomic rename (so it acts once), and calls only `ctx.session.prompt` (`delivery: "steer"`, with a fixed message id so a retry is never added twice) or `ctx.session.interrupt`. An interrupt flag older than 2 minutes is dropped unread; unclaimed messages are deleted after a day. Interrupt needs the local link, like every agent's; Reply also works over the relay. The plugin advertises what this OpenCode can do in the sealed blob (`controls`), and OpenCode 1.x never does, so the phone offers neither there. Nothing is executed as a shell command, and no process is started. Only a watchdog of this version or newer can route these commands, so while OpenCode runs the plugin checks every 15 s (one pidfile read and a `kill(pid, 0)`) and, when an older plugin's watchdog holds the queue, replaces it through the usual highest-version-wins handoff. It never stops a watchdog it could not replace. A message a watchdog cannot route gets an `x` (refused) receipt. - `/nomo-update` acts only on Nomo's own checkout: the stub's target must be an absolute `/plugin/dist/opencode.js` and the checkout's `origin` must be this repo on github.com (`https://`, `ssh://` or `git@github.com:`), or it refuses before running anything there. `bunx nomo-ai` updates global scope only, from your home directory, so the folder you run it in can never pick the checkout. - `opencode-install.sh` refuses to overwrite a same-named file it did not write (`--force` overrides). ### Cursor hooks - **Read-only by construction.** Eight events, **no permission hook**; the hook prints nothing and always exits 0, so it cannot allow, deny or redirect anything. `beforeSubmitPrompt` is awaited by Cursor, so a prompt can be **delayed** by one HTTPS request — at most ~2 s when the relay is unreachable. - **`hooks.json` is merged, never clobbered.** The installer refuses before writing if the file is not valid JSON of the expected shape, is a dangling symlink, has more than one hard link, or it or the skills directory is not writable; if a same-named skill it did not write exists (`--force` overrides); if the Cursor config directory is missing; or if `plugin/dist/` is not built. A live symlink is written through. It appends an entry only if that exact entry is absent, adds `"version": 1` only if missing, and never edits, reorders or removes an entry it did not write — an entry is Nomo's only if it is on one of its eight events, its command is exactly Nomo's two quoted paths under one checkout, and it has no keys besides `command` and `timeout`. A changed file is re-serialised as 2-space JSON (entries, key order and positions kept); an unchanged file is not rewritten. Writes are atomic (temp + rename) with the file's existing mode, re-reading just before the rename so another tool's concurrent write is merged. A checkout path containing `'`, `"`, `$`, `\` or a backtick is refused. Uninstall removes exactly Nomo's entries and skills. - The account email in Cursor's hook payloads is never read and is in no frame, record or log. ### Antigravity hooks - **Status hooks observe only, except to end a turn you interrupted or hand over a message you sent.** Nomo's `"nomo"` block answers every status event with `{}` before running anything — except `PostInvocation`, whose wrapper prints `{"terminationBehavior":"terminate"}` only when the bundle printed exactly that, which it does only after consuming a fresh interrupt flag the watchdog wrote from an `interrupt-session` command sealed by your paired phone (decrypted, fresh, never replayed, naming a session this computer tracks). - **Phone replies** take the same path: a sealed `send-message` command (same gates, a message id, at most 4,000 characters, no control characters but line breaks) becomes one owner-only `.agy-inbox` file. Only while such a file exists for the hook's own conversation do `PreInvocation` and `Stop` run in the foreground (capped at 4 s; the wrapper stops waiting at the bundle's first line, before any network call) and the wrapper prints that line only if it is exactly `{"injectSteps":[{"userMessage":"…"}…]}` (PreInvocation) or `{"decision":"continue","reason":"…"}` (Stop), else `{}`. A Stop continues at most once a minute, never for a turn your phone is stopping; unclaimed messages are deleted after a day. The only process Nomo ever starts for a reply is `agy --conversation --print=` (message as one argument, never shell-parsed), for a tracked `agy` CLI conversation whose `agy` has exited, in that conversation's folder. `agy` is found via `NOMO_AGY_BIN`, else the first **absolute** `PATH` entry holding one, else `~/.local/bin/agy`. Nomo never signals the `agy` process. - **The approval hook can only defer, approve what you approved, or deny what you denied or interrupted.** One `PreToolUse` entry, matched only to `run_command`, `write_file`, `write_to_file`, `edit_file`, `replace_file_content`, `multi_replace_file_content`. Antigravity treats a failing `PreToolUse` hook as a block, so `antigravity-approve.sh` passes through only Nomo's three replies (`allow`, `auto_approve`, `deny` with a reason) and answers `{"decision":"allow"}` — "no opinion": Antigravity's own settings and prompt — for anything else (crash, no runtime, malformed output, missing script, or a hold outliving its internal kill guard, which fires before the 24 h timeout). A signal mid-hold ends the hold, withdraws the card and leaves no process. `auto_approve` is sent only for an Allow sealed by your paired phone for that exact request id. Nomo never sends `permissionOverrides`, `overwrite` or a changed tool input. An interrupt flag makes it answer `deny` ("Stopped from phone"). - **Your `permissions` rules come first** (`settings.json` in that conversation's Antigravity data dir; both CLI and desktop dirs when unclear; read-only), in Antigravity's order Deny > Ask > Allow. Deny and ask rules are read **loosely**: a command rule matches when its command appears anywhere as something that runs — after `sudo`/`env`/`xargs`/`timeout`/`watch`/`stdbuf`/`nice`/`nohup`, inside `sh -c`/`bash -c`/`zsh -c` or `eval`, after `find -exec`, `then` or `!`, as `/bin/rm`, quoted, behind `FOO=1`, after `;`/`&&`/`|`, or inside `$(…)`; a `regex:` rule that does not compile matches everything. A call a deny rule may match never reaches the phone, and a phone Allow can never override it. File paths are normalized (`..`, `.`, repeated `/`) first. Allow rules are read **strictly**: only a single plain command (no separators, subshells, quotes or line breaks) whose words start with the rule's passes straight through, and never a write into Nomo's checkout or state folder. - **One sandbox-retry exception:** after a phone Allow on a shell command, the next call in the same conversation and workspace within 90 s whose arguments are identical except `BypassSandbox`, the one-line summary and the async wait time (the desktop app's retry outside its sandbox) is answered `auto_approve` once, without a new card. Any other difference gets a fresh card; never after a Deny; the one-use ticket is a `0600` file in the sessions folder. - **Own commands:** so that `/nomo-status` doesn't put a card on your phone, the approval hook answers `auto_approve` — on a paired computer, after the deny rules and a pending Stop — for exactly four command lines rebuilt in code from the template the installer writes the skills from (never read from the skill files): status (plain and verbose), approvals status and approvals **on**. Byte-for-byte match (one trailing newline forgiven; a second line, a `cd`, `&& …` or other quoting goes to the phone). Approvals **off**, pair, the pair wait, reset, unpair and the typed pairing code still ask your phone: on a paired computer, pairing again first revokes the current pairing. - **What it reads.** The approval hook: tool name, `CommandLine` or file path, and the model's `toolSummary` (sent sealed). Status events: only `conversationId`, the first `workspacePaths` entry, `transcriptPath` (its mtime and first line) and `modelName` — never tool arguments. From `conversation_summaries.db`: only `title`, `status` and `last_modified_time` of that conversation, read-only; the id must be UUID-shaped before it enters the query, and only the two Antigravity data dirs are read. - **Installer.** Owns exactly the `"nomo"` block in `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (rewritten whole; other blocks untouched; file created as `{}` if absent; refuses a file that is not a JSON object; writes through a symlink). Each registered command first checks its script exists and otherwise answers on its own (`{}`, or `{"decision":"allow"}` for `PreToolUse`), so a moved or deleted `~/.nomo` never blocks a tool. The plugin folder carries a marker file; an unmarked `nomo` folder is someone else's and the installer refuses. The `/nomo-*` skills run only Nomo's own local commands and never print the pairing link or QR secret. Uninstall deletes only that block and the marked folder. ### Devin hooks - **The status hook observes only, except to end a turn you interrupted.** It prints nothing — except that after you tap **Interrupt**, its next `PostToolUse` prints `{"continue":false,"stopReason":"Interrupted from Nomo"}` (the watchdog writes the flag only for an interrupt sealed by your paired phone; the next prompt clears it). From each event it reads only `session_id`, `prompt_id`, the event and tool names, the first prompt (for the title) and `DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR`; from Devin's `sessions.db` only that session's `title`, `model` and `working_directory`, read-only (the id must be a plain slug before it enters the query). - **The approval hook can only defer, approve what you approved, deny what you denied, or pass on your answer.** On `PermissionRequest` it sends the tool name and command or file path sealed, and prints `{"decision":"approve"}` only for an Allow sealed by your paired phone for that exact request id (`{"decision":"block"}` with your note, or "Denied from phone", for a Deny). On `PreToolUse` it holds only `ask_user_question`: questions and options go sealed to the phone, and your answer comes back as `{"decision":"block","reason":"The user answered from their phone (Nomo): …"}` — Devin has no way to take an answer from a hook, so the model reads the decline reason as your answer and the transcript shows the question as rejected. A Deny is a block saying you chose not to answer. **Fail-open:** unpaired, approvals paused, session not on the phone, offline, expiry, crash or timeout all print nothing, leaving Devin's own prompt. If Devin stops waiting (its timeout, Ctrl-C, session end), the hook notices its parent shell is gone, withdraws the card and exits. - **"Always allow (this session)"** is stored only on this computer in `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/.devin-allow` and forgotten when the session ends (or Nomo retires its quiet row), and every one is deleted by unpair, by reset, and when you pair again. While it exists, and only while this computer is paired, a matching request in that session is approved at once, even with approvals paused. A shell grant covers the command's name only for a short list of tools whose arguments cannot run code (`ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `touch`, `mkdir`, `grep`, `echo`, `pwd`, `which`, `file`, `stat`, `du`, `cut`, `tr`, `jq`), typed as the bare name, with no shell operators, no glob (`*`, `?`, `[`) and no Devin Desktop `workdir` (`touch` covers `touch b.txt`, not `touchy` or `./touch`). Such a grant still lets `cat`, `grep` or `jq` read any file you can read. Every other command — shells, interpreters, `git`, `make`, `rg`, build tools, agents, `cp`, `rm`, anything with `&&`, `;`, `|`, `$(…)`, backticks or a redirect — is covered only by a grant for that exact text: `git status` does not cover `git -c core.fsmonitor=… status`, and `touch x && rm -rf ~` still asks. An exact grant re-runs that text as-is, in any folder, and does not pin what it runs (`make test` runs whatever the Makefile says then). A shell grant never matches a request carrying any key besides the command and `workdir`. Nomo's own pair, unpair, reset, disable and uninstall commands, and commands whose text or `workdir` names its state folders (`~/.config/cc-status`, `~/.nomo`), are never approved by a grant; quoting tricks are normalized, but a glob can still slip past that check in an exact grant's text (a glob never gets or uses a name grant). For any other tool it covers that tool for the session. - **Own commands:** on a paired computer, before any card, Nomo auto-approves exactly three command lines, rebuilt in code and matched byte for byte against what the skills run (the plugin's `/nomo:*` and the installer's `/nomo-*` forms, with at most Devin Desktop's `workdir` beside them): status, approvals status and approvals **on**. One trailing newline is forgiven; any other difference (`&& …`, `;`, `|`, a redirect, a second line, another script or path, an extra argument) goes to the phone. Approvals **off**, pair, the pair wait, reset, unpair and the typed pairing code still ask your phone: on a paired computer, pairing again first revokes the current pairing. - **Writes.** Devin's own config files are never written by the hooks. The installer writes only its entries in the `"hooks"` key and the marked `nomo-*` skills (which run only Nomo's local commands and never print the pairing link or QR secret); a same-named skill of yours is left alone. A `config.json` with comments is first copied to `config.json.nomo-backup`, then written back without them. The plugin registers the same two bundles through its `hooks.json`, adds no rules, MCP servers or agents, and declares `"platforms": ["local"]`; while the installer's entries are present its copies exit without sending anything. Uninstall removes only Nomo's entries and marked skills. - Devin Desktop's **Restricted Mode** turns hooks off, and Nomo with them. ### Runtime and launch - **Your project's runtime config is never loaded.** Hooks run with your project as working folder, and bun reads `bunfig.toml` (whose `preload` runs code) and `.env` from there. Whenever the runtime is bun, Nomo starts it with `--config=/dev/null --env-file=/dev/null`, including for processes it starts itself (the watchdog). Node reads neither and is started as-is. The working folder is left alone, so version managers (asdf, mise, proto, nodenv) keep working. - **Only installed copies run.** The version-stable hook shim runs the copy that last ran, or the newest installed copy in the Claude Code / Codex plugin cache — never code from a marketplace you added but did not install. - **Runtime floor.** bun before 1.4.4 and Node.js 22 before 22.23.4 are affected by CVE-2026-111497 (brotli decompression). The status commands and the `nomo-ai` installer print a warning naming the runtime and how to upgrade; hooks keep running. - **LAN listener.** Plain HTTP on the local network; the `K_lan` seal is the security boundary. Every rejection is an empty `400` so a prober cannot tell wrong key from stale timestamp from "no pairing here"; requests carry a timestamp and nonce, body size is capped, and commands are still validated (allow-list, freshness, replay dedupe) exactly as on the relay path. ## How it works Every integration runs from one shared `plugin/` directory: a **Claude Code plugin** (`nomo-cc`), a **native Codex plugin** (`nomo`), an **OpenCode plugin module**, and hooks merged into **Cursor**, **Antigravity** and **Devin** config (Devin can also use a native plugin). The hooks, watchdog and commands are single-file `.mjs` bundles that run under **bun or node ≥ 18** (`run.sh` picks whichever is installed); OpenCode loads one resident `.js` bundle. **Zero npm dependencies.** - **Pairing.** `pair` writes a themed local page with a QR and one-time code, derives the key as in [Architecture](#architecture), and writes `~/.config/cc-status/config.json` (`0600`). Every agent reads that same file, so one pairing covers them all and an unpaired hook is a no-op. - **Hook.** Each lifecycle event plans a v2 op (`start` / `update` / `done` / `end` with a `working` / `needsAttention` / `done` status), seals the payload, and POSTs it to the relay, which pushes via APNs. A POST the 2 s timeout cuts off marks the record `updatePending`. - **Liveness watchdog.** Closing a terminal kills the agent with no end event. Each event records `sessions/.json` with the agent's pid; one detached `cc-watchdog.mjs` polls every 5 s and POSTs a corrective `end` once that pid is dead (Codex interrupts are read from the rollout transcript). It re-sends `updatePending` records with a 5 s timeout, backing off 5 s → 60 s after a failure and holding back while an approval hold is live. With no sessions it lingers, while paired, up to 30 min (`IDLE_GRACE_MS`), and the next hook re-spawns it. - **LAN fast path.** When the phone is on the same network, the watchdog hosts a small HTTP listener so commands and answers arrive in <200 ms instead of riding the next relay response (~5–12 s). It is strictly additive: the relay leg runs in parallel and stays canonical, so any LAN failure means "the relay wins", never a lost command. Off by default; turned on in the app. State lives under `~/.config/cc-status/`. `NOMO_WORKER_URL` at pair time points at a staging Worker. ### Claude Code integration Hooks: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Notification`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, `StopFailure`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Elicitation`, `ElicitationResult` — wired by the plugin. Claude Code auto-updates third-party marketplaces only when their `autoUpdate` flag is on (off by default), so `claude plugin update nomo-cc@nomo` is what moves an install. ### Codex integration Codex **≥ 0.142** native plugin `nomo`, sharing `plugin/` with the Claude manifest. Hooks: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Interrupt`. Its blob is tagged `agent: "codex"` inside the seal. `request_user_input` questions need the Codex task and the Nomo watchdog to share one app-server process. Codex has no plugin update verb: with a `local` marketplace (`source_type` in `~/.codex/config.toml`, the common case) Codex reads the plugin live from the path; with `git`, `codex plugin marketplace upgrade ` refreshes the snapshot. ### OpenCode integration - No marketplace, no hooks: OpenCode auto-discovers `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}`, so `opencode-install.sh` writes `~/.config/opencode/plugins/nomo.js` — a one-line stub **re-exporting** `/plugin/dist/opencode.js` (so the bundle executes beside its sibling `cc-watchdog.mjs`) — and the six `commands/nomo-*.md` with the plugin path baked in. `--project` targets `./.opencode/`. - Deliberately **no npm-resolved plugin**: OpenCode's `Npm.add` short-circuits on an existing cache directory, so a package spec resolves `@latest` once and never updates. The **checkout is the version**, which is why the installer needs a durable `~/.nomo` clone rather than a `bunx` cache. - `/nomo-update` reads its checkout back out of the stub, fetches, reads the target version with `git show :plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (nothing checked out), and only if behind fast-forwards and re-runs the installer. It refuses on a `--ref` pin (detached), a dirty tree, no upstream, diverged history, unreachable remote, or a moved stub. - Plugins are imported once at server start (no hot reload), and the plugin reads the pairing then — so pairing from inside OpenCode needs a restart. The blob is tagged `agent: "opencode"`. Todo lists ride along as plan detail. "Open on Mac" works for the desktop app only (`opencodeLocateTuiPid` walks the server's ancestry for `/OpenCode.app/Contents/MacOS/`). Auto vs. manual approval mode is TUI state that never crosses HTTP, so it is not shown. With `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLAN_MODE` off a plan turn shows only "Planning"; with it on, `plan_exit` arrives as a normal question. Liveness is the OpenCode server process. `opencode --pure` starts without external plugins. - **2.x:** events come from `ctx.event.subscribe` and are translated into the 1.x shapes the plugin already handles (`src/opencode/v2.ts`), so the phone sees the same records either way. The stream is server-wide, so events for other folders are dropped. By default 2.x runs plugins in its background service, not the TUI, so the row's liveness is that service: closing the TUI leaves a finished row, ended when the service stops. A row waiting on a question or a permission the phone cannot answer is closed (`end`, no "finished" alert) about 10–20 s after the last OpenCode window detaches from that service (or from a plain `opencode serve`): the plugin counts the connections into the server's own listening port (`lsof`), since 2.x has no client-presence event. OpenCode keeps the prompt pending; answer it in a reopened window and the row comes back. An Allow/Deny card on the phone is never closed this way, and a running turn is left alone. A background subagent can still be running after the parent's turn shows done; the done frame counts them (`bgAgents`). Other 2.x states ride sealed too: a retry's next attempt time and whether it is rate limiting (`retryAt`, `retryReason`), compaction (`phase`), and a failed or interrupted turn (`outcome`); see [docs/opencode-2x-remote-contract.md](docs/opencode-2x-remote-contract.md). 2.x only produces todos when its `todo` flag is on (`OPENCODE_FLAGS=todo` or `experimental.todo: true`). ### Cursor integration - One user-level `hooks.json` serves both the desktop app and `cursor-agent`. Events: `sessionStart`, `beforeSubmitPrompt`, `postToolUse`, `postToolUseFailure`, `afterShellExecution`, `afterFileEdit`, `stop`, `sessionEnd`. Commands are Cursor skills (`~/.cursor/skills/nomo-*/SKILL.md`). - Status-only: no hold, no answer, and no `locateTuiPid` seam, so a session is only *working* or *done*. - A row starts at `beforeSubmitPrompt`, and only a new prompt reopens a stopped turn. - The title is Cursor's own chat name, one field read read-only with the system `sqlite3` from the desktop app's state database; until then, and for `cursor-agent` chats, the first prompt. - A turn with no `stop` is marked done after 30 quiet minutes; a finished row retires after a little over an hour and returns to working on new activity. - Updating is a `git pull --ff-only` of `~/.nomo` plus a re-run of `cursor-install.mjs`. ### Antigravity integration - `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` serves both the desktop app and the `agy` CLI. Status events `SessionStart`, `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, `Stop`, `PostToolUse` run `antigravity-hook.sh ` (10 s timeout); `PreToolUse` runs `antigravity-approve.sh` (24 h). The plugin in `~/.gemini/config/plugins/nomo` carries only skills — plugin-packaged hooks reach only the CLI. An imported `nomo-cc` would report every session twice; the installer says so but never removes it. - A row starts at `PreInvocation`. `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation` and `PostToolUse` keep it working (throttled); `Stop` marks it done. A turn that ends with no event is settled by the watchdog once the hook's parent process is gone and Antigravity's conversation index shows the run idle after the last event; the 30-minute reap is the last resort. - **Interrupt** stamps a one-shot flag for that conversation (needs the local link); the next `PostInvocation` ends the turn after the current model call or tool. Flags unused within an hour, or left when the turn ended on its own, are dropped; Antigravity's flags are separate from Claude Code's. - **Reply** (up to 4,000 characters, sealed, over LAN and relay) is queued per conversation and handed over at the next `PreInvocation`; a message arriving during the last step makes that turn's `Stop` continue once. The phone shows *Queued* then *Delivered* and can cancel until then. A finished, exited `agy` conversation is resumed with `agy --conversation --print=…`; an `agy` still open keeps the message for your next turn; a finished desktop conversation continues only on the Mac. An Interrupt always wins. - Approval outcomes: Allow → `auto_approve`; Deny → `deny` with your note; everything else → `allow` ("no opinion"). "Always allow" is not offered. If Antigravity cancels the hook mid-hold, the card is withdrawn within seconds and the row returns to working. - The title is `title` from `conversation_summaries.db` in `~/.gemini/antigravity` (desktop) or `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` (`agy`), available after the first turn; before that, the first prompt from the transcript, then the workspace folder. The model badge is `modelName`. ### Devin integration - Two install routes for the Devin CLI and Devin Desktop's Devin Local: the installer (hooks merged into `~/.config/devin/config.json`, read by both) or the native plugin (`.devin-plugin/plugin.json`, `"platforms": ["local"]`, never runs in Devin cloud sessions). If both are present the installer's entries win and the plugin stands down ("both installed — plugin idle" in status). - Hooks: status on `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd` (10 s); approval on `PermissionRequest` and `PreToolUse` matched to `^ask_user_question$` (24 h). Commands are skills — `/nomo:*` from the plugin, `/nomo-*` from the installer. - Interrupt (local link) ends the turn after the current step; Devin cannot cut a command or reply off halfway. While the phone holds a prompt, Devin Desktop shows no buttons of its own for it (like Claude Code's terminal). In Desktop's default Code mode Devin asks only for commands, web fetches and writes outside the project. ### Installer (`nomo-ai`) - A **bootstrapper, not a package manager**: it drives each host's own install path and never writes into `~/.claude` or `~/.codex` itself — a second writer racing `claude plugin update` is how two versions end up fighting over one watchdog. The npm package ships only `bin/`, not the plugin bundle. - With no flags and no terminal it refuses rather than guessing; every failure names the step, exit code and the command to run by hand, and the exit status is non-zero if any agent failed. - Updates: OpenCode, Cursor, Antigravity and Devin legs update `~/.nomo` themselves (the checkout is the version). Claude Code and Codex rows only **print** the host command, because install begins with `marketplace add`, which would silently repoint a marketplace you aimed elsewhere (a fork, a local checkout). A Codex `local` marketplace prints nothing, since there is nothing to run. - **Commands** (`pair`, `status`, `reset`, `unpair`) run the INSTALLED plugin's own entry, not code from the npm package: the highest plugin version among every installed copy — the copy named in the hook shim's stamp (`~/.config/cc-status`), `~/.nomo`, and each version in the Claude Code / Codex plugin caches (the same copies the hook shim considers; superseded Codex copies are skipped) — through that copy's `run.sh`, so the runtime rules in [Runtime and launch](#runtime-and-launch) apply. Nothing installed → one line saying to run `bunx nomo-ai` first. Output and exit status are the entry's own. An unknown word is refused, never treated as an install. - **Short command.** Installed without asking once Nomo is installed (also under `-y`), skipped with `--no-global`, and not reinstalled when this version is already on PATH. It runs exactly `bun add -g nomo-ai` or `npm install -g nomo-ai` (shown first; `-n` only shows it), never with `sudo`, and a failure never changes the exit status. A `nomo` already on PATH counts as this package only if it resolves to `bin/nomo-ai.mjs` beside a `package.json` named `nomo-ai`; any other `nomo` is left alone and never run. The outcome goes to `~/.config/cc-status/short-command`, which the plugin's own output reads (no PATH probe); with no record it names both forms. - `--ref ` applies only to the `~/.nomo` checkout (Claude/Codex marketplaces read the default branch, and the installer says so). The checkout is left **detached** so a later plain run recognises the pin and refuses to fast-forward it. ## Development Sources live in `src/`: `entries/` (bundled entrypoints), `core/` (paths/config, E2E crypto, the hook op planner, agent adapters), `opencode/` (the resident module), `qr/` (vendored QR encoder). All run unmodified under **bun and node ≥ 18** — no `Bun.*` runtime APIs, no npm dependencies. ### Tests ``` bun test ``` Runs the full suite across `core/`, `entries/`, `opencode/` and `qr/`. ### Building the plugin bundle ``` bun build.ts ``` Bundles every hook/command entrypoint in `src/entries/` into `plugin/dist/*.mjs`, inlining local imports so each is one node-runnable file. A second pass bundles `src/opencode/plugin.ts` into `plugin/dist/opencode.js` — **`.js`, not `.mjs`**, because OpenCode's discovery glob is `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}`; it has no `hooks.json` entry and no `hook-shim.sh` row. The OpenCode commands are templates: `plugin/opencode-commands/*.md` (filename = command name) carry a `__NOMO_ROOT__` placeholder that `opencode-install.sh` replaces with the plugin path — OpenCode offers no `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` equivalent. A new `.md` there is picked up with no code change. `plugin/dist/` **is committed.** Marketplace installs are a plain `git clone` with no CI build step, so the committed bundle is what runs. Re-run `bun build.ts` after any source change and commit the result; it was built with `bun 1.3.14` — use the same major/minor to reproduce it byte for byte. ### Releasing The version lives in manifests that must move together (deliberately not repeated here — prose drifts, and `build.ts` checks only the JSON): - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude Code marketplace) - `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` (Codex marketplace) - `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (`nomo-cc`) - `plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` (`nomo`) - `package.json` (the `nomo-ai` npm bootstrapper) - `.devin-plugin/plugin.json` (the native Devin plugin, `nomo`) OpenCode has no manifest; its checkout is its version. `bun build.ts` refuses to build when the six disagree. `package.json` carries the version only so `bunx nomo-ai --version` is quotable in a bug report. The npm publish is manual — `npm pack --dry-run` first: the tarball is `bin/` plus `package.json`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`, nothing else. ## Contributors Thank you to everyone who helped make Nomo better: - [@tecandrew](https://github.com/tecandrew): worked out the OpenCode 2.x plugin migration and shared a working adapter, which became OpenCode 2.x support in plugin 2.5.2. ## License — MIT Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). © 2026 KarrixLee.

# Nomo — Live Activity on your iPhone

                 

Nomo mirrors your **Claude Code**, **OpenAI Codex** (CLI and desktop app), **OpenCode**, **Cursor**, **Antigravity** and **Devin** sessions to the Nomo iPhone app as a Live Activity — working, needs you, done — and lets you answer permission prompts and questions from the phone. Everything is end-to-end encrypted; one pairing covers every agent on a computer. This README is the **technical and security reference**. How to install, pair, use the commands, update and uninstall lives at **[docs.nomo.gg](https://docs.nomo.gg)**. > [!NOTE] > Developed and tested on **macOS** and **Linux**. **Windows is untested** (the hooks are pure Node > built-ins, but nothing has been verified there), so treat it as unsupported. ## Security at a glance - **End-to-end encrypted.** Every session update is sealed with **AES-256-GCM** on your computer and opened only on your iPhone. The key comes from pairing (QR secret or six-word code, then a per-pairing ephemeral **ECDH P-256** exchange) and never passes through a server. [Encryption](#encryption) - **The relay is blind.** The Cloudflare Worker that forwards pushes sees routing metadata only — never a title, machine name, status text, command or answer. The one thing it sees in the clear is the presence ping (once a minute, and when it changes): which agents have a turn open, and whether one is waiting for approval. A free (not Pro) pairing sends only that ping and the sealed daily activity summary, except that after a quiet spell the first prompt's requests still go out (end-to-end encrypted, as always) and are refused. [What leaves your computer](#what-leaves-your-computer) - **No telemetry, no credentials.** The plugin's only network peer is that relay (`https://api.nomo.gg` by default). It never reads your agents' API keys or logins, and has no analytics. The installer and `/nomo-update` also run `git` against `github.com/KarrixLee/nomo`. [Network](#network) - **Hooks can only do what you answered.** A phone Allow, Deny or answer is acted on only when it is sealed by your paired phone for that exact request. Every failure — unpaired, offline, timeout, crash — **fails open** to the agent's own prompt. Nomo can delay a decision; it never makes one for you, except auto-approving its **own** status commands, matched byte for byte. Nomo's own pair, unpair, reset and uninstall commands always ask. [Hooks security](#hooks-security) - **Phone commands are sealed and narrow.** Interrupt, Reply (Antigravity, OpenCode 2.x) and Open on Mac run only when sealed by your paired phone, fresh (under 2 minutes) and never replayed, for a session this computer tracks. A reply is handed to the agent as a user message; nothing from the phone is ever run as a shell command. [OpenCode 2.x remote control](#opencode-plugin) - **Local files are owner-only.** Pairing keys and session records live in `~/.config/cc-status/`, written `0600`. Every file Nomo writes into an agent's config is listed below, and the installers merge rather than overwrite. It can be handed over two ways, both keeping it off every server: - **Scan the QR** on the local pairing page. The QR carries a random pairing secret that exists only in the code image; the phone mixes it with its own nonce (HKDF-SHA256). - **Type the one-time code** — six words and a channel number (e.g. `7-ocean-sunset-mango-river-atlas-cabin`). The phone runs PBKDF2-SHA256 over the words to rebuild the same secret, then the same HKDF step. The words never leave the pairing page; the channel is a one-time routing handle that burns on first use and expires in 10 minutes. The plugin seals every update before it leaves the machine; the relay Worker and Apple's push service carry ciphertext only, and the iPhone decrypts (for the Live Activity, in the widget at render time). Diagram source: [`assets/architecture.excalidraw`](assets/architecture.excalidraw) — open it at [excalidraw.com](https://excalidraw.com) to edit. ### The pairing code is never printed By default the one-time code is shown **only on the pairing page** (a local `file://` page, `0600`, with no fonts, remote images, analytics or CDN), behind "Tap to reveal code". It is never printed to the terminal, so it cannot land in shell history, a screen recording or an AI transcript. `pair.mjs --show-code` (the `pair code` form of each agent's pair command) is the deliberate opt-out for a headless or SSH-only box: it prints the code to stdout, where it is sensitive for the ~10 minutes it is valid. The page is deleted when pairing completes. ## Encryption - **AES-256-GCM** seals every session update, approval card and answer. The relay can route by pairing id but cannot read a field. - **Six BIP39 words (~66 bits)**, stretched with **PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations** (salted with the pairing id), put an offline brute-force of the code — what a logging relay could try against the known-plaintext pairing blob — out of reach. - **Forward secrecy via a per-pairing ephemeral ECDH (P-256) ratchet.** The QR secret or code only bootstraps a handshake key. Computer and phone each generate a throwaway keypair, do an ECDH, and mix the result with the bootstrap key into the key that encrypts your sessions; the throwaway private keys are discarded after pairing. A code leaked **after** pairing cannot decrypt anything, and mixing it into the handshake means a relay that swaps the public keys (man-in-the-middle) makes pairing fail rather than succeed under its key. Only public keys transit the relay in the clear. - **Each sealed update names its own session.** The session id travels in the clear for routing, so the sealed blob repeats it (`sid`). The app treats a blob whose sealed `sid` differs from the session it is listed under as unreadable, so a relay cannot relabel one session's update as another's and steer an approval or interrupt onto the wrong session. (Plugins older than this send no `sid`; their updates are still shown.) - **LAN fast path has its own seal.** Local-network traffic is sealed under `K_lan` = HKDF-SHA256(pairing key, info `nomo-lan-v1|`), so nobody on the Wi-Fi can read even the metadata, and a relay ciphertext will not open on the LAN channel (or vice versa). See [LAN fast path](#lan-fast-path). ## What leaves your computer ### Network | Destination | When | What | |---|---|---| | Relay Worker (`https://api.nomo.gg`, or `NOMO_WORKER_URL` at pair time) | every session event; approval holds; pairing; unpair; the activity summary; presence about once a minute while an agent session is open, plus one when it changes (at most every ~27 s) | `/v1/cc/event`, `/v1/cc/decision*`, `/v1/cc/full`, `/v1/cc/pair/*`, `/v1/cc/presence` | | Your iPhone, on the same network (only if LAN is turned on in the app) | commands and answers | `POST /v1/lan`, sealed under `K_lan` | | `github.com/KarrixLee/nomo` via `git` | `bunx nomo-ai` (OpenCode, Cursor, Antigravity, Devin legs) and `/nomo-update` | clone / fetch / pull of this repo | | The npm registry, via your package manager | `bunx nomo-ai`, for the short `nomo` command (skip with `--no-global`) | `bun add -g nomo-ai` or `npm install -g nomo-ai` | Nothing else: no analytics, no crash reporting, no reads of agent credentials. **In the clear to the relay** (needed to route and authenticate): the pairing id and the computer's pairing secret (headers), the plugin version, whether remote approvals are on, and per event the session id, the op (`start` / `update` / `done` / `end`), a priority, timestamps, and — for a Codex `request_user_input` question only — `attentionKind: "userInput"`. **Sealed**: everything else — title, machine name, folder, status, model, tool name, command, file path, plan text, questions, answers, and which agent produced the event. It **never** puts prompt or reply text, project names or paths into the summary. To send it right away, run `nomo reset` (or reset inside your agent: `/nomo-cc:reset`, `$nomo-reset`, `/nomo-reset`): it scans and uploads once, then says whether it was sent. The relay cannot read them and deletes them after **35 days**. The summary carries a random per-computer id (`mid`) so the phone does not count a computer twice — a UUID made once and kept in `~/.config/cc-status/machine-id` (owner-only), **never** derived from serial, MAC, hostname or user name; delete the file for a new one. **Presence — two fields, every pairing.** About once a minute while the watchdog runs (an agent session is open), and as soon as the answer changes (never more than once per ~27 s), the plugin POSTs `/v1/cc/presence` with `{ "coding": [agent ids], "waiting": true|false }` plus one `"agent"` + `"pluginVersion"` pair (each agent's own Nomo integration version, one agent per POST in turn; left off against a relay that does not take them yet): which agents (`claude`, `codex`, …) have a turn open, and whether any session is waiting for an approval. No session id, title, folder, command or text. It is not sealed (the relay keeps it about 3 minutes so the phone can show "Claude is coding"), and the reply tells the plugin whether the pairing is Pro. **Free pairing (not Pro) — only presence and the activity summary leave the computer.** When the relay says a pairing is not Pro (the presence reply, or a 403 `{"error":"entitlement suspended"}` on any session route — or, from a relay that says so, the claim itself at pairing time), the plugin writes `~/.config/cc-status/free-mode` (removed on unpair, re-pair and a revoke teardown) and, while it is fresh (15 minutes, refreshed by each presence reply), sends **no** session events, opens **no** approval holds (every prompt goes straight to the agent's own dialog), uploads **no** plan or permission text, and keys the LAN listener off. Sessions are still tracked on disk so presence stays accurate. After a quiet spell (15 minutes with no presence reply) the marker has expired, so the first prompt's sealed requests go out (one event; on a permission prompt also the full text and the approval request), the relay refuses them and stores nothing, and free mode resumes. The LAN listener does not come back when the marker expires: it stays keyed off until the relay says the pairing is Pro (a presence reply, or an accepted session request), which deletes the marker. A 403 is never treated as an unpair (only a 404/410 is), and neither is a `409` (a pairing the relay has not seen claimed yet): a session event is retried later, and a prompt's approval request falls open to the agent's own prompt, as on any other relay error. **On the iPhone,** the Live Agents widget (Nomo Pro) reads a snapshot of decrypted titles, states and computer names from the app's own App Group container. the answer rides back sealed, so the relay never learns what you chose. - **Fail-open.** A network error, timeout or unpaired state before the hold is granted drops straight to the agent's own dialog. Once granted, a failed poll counts as a miss; ~5 minutes of consecutive misses gives up the same way. While the relay is reachable the hold has no ceiling of its own — it waits until you answer, the request expires or is superseded server-side, or the hook is killed (Esc at the terminal, or the agent's hook timeout). - **Approvals switch.** One machine-wide flag pauses remote approvals for every agent; prompts then go straight to the computer. - **Free pairings never hold.** While the pairing is not Pro (see [What leaves your computer](#what-leaves-your-computer)) every prompt goes straight to the agent's own dialog, exactly like the paused switch, and nothing is posted. - **Shell cards keep the command.** The model-written one-line description is a caption: shortened first, and dropped before the command when space runs out. - **The "Always allow" label is display-only.** At hold time the plugin seals what an Always-allow tap would grant into the card as `permissionGrant`: structured data, never prose, so the phone builds the label in its own language. Format: `""`, or one or more entries joined by `\n`, each `kind` or `kind:literal` (the literal is everything after the first `:`, has no control characters, is capped at 80 characters, and the phone shows it verbatim in monospace, never as Markdown). Kinds: `cmd:` (commands starting with it, or a Claude Code rule with a `*` wildcard shown as written), `exact` (this exact command), `domain:`, `edit:`, `dir:` (one folder), `dirs:` (N folders), `edits`, `reads`, `fetches`, `searches`, `commands` (every one of that kind), `planmode`, `automode`, `plans` (plan approvals), `tool:` (the whole tool) and `similar` (a rule the plugin can't name; also how the phone shows a kind it doesn't know). Any unnamed part, or a value over 240 characters, collapses to `similar`, never a shorter list. It is built from the same input as the answer: Claude Code's own suggestions (after the filter below), OpenCode's `always` patterns, or Devin's Nomo-side grant rule. `""` means the tap would only be a one-time allow, and the phone hides the option; absent (Codex, Antigravity, questions, older plugins) means unknown. It only labels the button: the rule itself is still decided and enforced by the agent. - **Claude Code Computer Use** app-access dialogs fire no answerable hook, so the phone shows a sealed heads-up naming the apps with no Allow/Deny; approve it on the computer. ### Claude Code hooks - Wired by the plugin's `hooks.json` (no `settings.json` edits). Status hooks are silent: unpaired → no-op; relay down → 2 s POST timeout, exit 0. They cannot affect the session. - `PermissionRequest` (timeout 24 h) is the only hook that answers. **"Always allow (this session)" stays in this session:** Claude Code often marks its suggested rules (e.g. `Bash(bun test:*)`) to be saved to `.claude/settings.local.json`; Nomo keeps the allow rules, extra directories and mode switches it suggested, rewrites every one to `destination: "session"`, and drops deny rules and the `bypassPermissions` / `dontAsk` modes. A phone tap never writes a settings file and the grant ends with the session. It never widens the suggestion: the whole-tool rule (e.g. plain `Read`) is used only when nothing was suggested; if everything suggested was dropped, the tap is a one-time allow. - Inside Devin (which also runs `~/.claude` hooks), Nomo's Claude Code hooks stand down, so a Devin session is never a Claude Code row and never answered by them. ### Codex hooks - The ten hooks ship in `plugin/hooks/codex-hooks.json` and stay **inert until you trust them** in Codex's `/hooks` review — Codex's own gate, which Nomo cannot pre-approve. One file serves OpenCode 1.x (`server`) and 2.x (`setup`). - **OpenCode 1.x:** it answers `permission.asked` (Allow / Always / Deny) and `question.asked`. **Always** is OpenCode's own `always` reply: it allows the request's `always` patterns (e.g. `git status *`, or `*` for every edit) for that project **until OpenCode restarts**, across its sessions — OpenCode keeps the rule in memory, never on disk. - **OpenCode 2.x:** it answers permissions through OpenCode's in-process `ctx.permission.reply`: Allow, **Always allow (saved for this project)**, Deny and **Deny with note**. 2.x saves an Always rule (the request's `save` patterns, e.g. `git status *`) to the project **on disk**, where it outlives restarts, so the card states it as `permissionProjectGrant` and only a phone that labels it "saved for this project" (app 2.5.3+) offers it; `permissionGrant` stays `""`, so an older app, whose OpenCode label says "until OpenCode restarts", keeps hiding Always. A note rides on the reject as OpenCode's `message`: the model reads it and keeps working (a plain Deny ends the step). A Deny rejects that request and every other one OpenCode raised in the same step (the same assistant message). Questions are 2.x forms, which plugins have no way to answer: the phone shows the session as waiting and you answer on the computer. - **OpenCode 2.x remote control — Reply and Interrupt.** These are new powers for your phone: **Reply** types a message into a session (as if you typed it in OpenCode), and **Interrupt** stops its running turn. Both arrive only as commands sealed by your paired phone and pass the watchdog's usual gates (decrypted under the pairing key, a kind on the allow-list, sealed less than 2 minutes ago, nonce never seen before, naming a session this computer tracks). The watchdog then leaves them as owner-only files in `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/`: a reply as one `.agy-inbox` file (at most 4,000 characters, no control characters but line breaks), an interrupt as `.oc-interrupt`. The plugin, inside OpenCode, checks once a second, acts only for sessions in its own folder, claims each file with an atomic rename (so it acts once), and calls only `ctx.session.prompt` (`delivery: "steer"`, with a fixed message id so a retry is never added twice) or `ctx.session.interrupt`. An interrupt flag older than 2 minutes is dropped unread; unclaimed messages are deleted after a day. Interrupt needs the local link, like every agent's; Reply also works over the relay. The plugin advertises what this OpenCode can do in the sealed blob (`controls`), and OpenCode 1.x never does, so the phone offers neither there. Nothing is executed as a shell command, and no process is started. Only a watchdog of this version or newer can route these commands, so while OpenCode runs the plugin checks every 15 s (one pidfile read and a `kill(pid, 0)`) and, when an older plugin's watchdog holds the queue, replaces it through the usual highest-version-wins handoff. It never stops a watchdog it could not replace. A message a watchdog cannot route gets an `x` (refused) receipt. - `/nomo-update` acts only on Nomo's own checkout: the stub's target must be an absolute `/plugin/dist/opencode.js` and the checkout's `origin` must be this repo on github.com (`https://`, `ssh://` or `git@github.com:`), or it refuses before running anything there. `bunx nomo-ai` updates global scope only, from your home directory, so the folder you run it in can never pick the checkout. - `opencode-install.sh` refuses to overwrite a same-named file it did not write (`--force` overrides). ### Cursor hooks - **Read-only by construction.** Eight events, **no permission hook**; the hook prints nothing and always exits 0, so it cannot allow, deny or redirect anything. `beforeSubmitPrompt` is awaited by Cursor, so a prompt can be **delayed** by one HTTPS request — at most ~2 s when the relay is unreachable. - **`hooks.json` is merged, never clobbered.** The installer refuses before writing if the file is not valid JSON of the expected shape, is a dangling symlink, has more than one hard link, or it or the skills directory is not writable; if a same-named skill it did not write exists (`--force` overrides); if the Cursor config directory is missing; or if `plugin/dist/` is not built. A live symlink is written through. It appends an entry only if that exact entry is absent, adds `"version": 1` only if missing, and never edits, reorders or removes an entry it did not write — an entry is Nomo's only if it is on one of its eight events, its command is exactly Nomo's two quoted paths under one checkout, and it has no keys besides `command` and `timeout`. A changed file is re-serialised as 2-space JSON (entries, key order and positions kept); an unchanged file is not rewritten. Writes are atomic (temp + rename) with the file's existing mode, re-reading just before the rename so another tool's concurrent write is merged. A checkout path containing `'`, `"`, `$`, `\` or a backtick is refused. A Stop continues at most once a minute, never for a turn your phone is stopping; unclaimed messages are deleted after a day. The only process Nomo ever starts for a reply is `agy --conversation --print=` (message as one argument, never shell-parsed), for a tracked `agy` CLI conversation whose `agy` has exited, in that conversation's folder. `agy` is found via `NOMO_AGY_BIN`, else the first **absolute** `PATH` entry holding one, else `~/.local/bin/agy`.
