A signal mid-hold ends the hold, withdraws the card and leaves no process. `auto_approve` is sent only for an Allow sealed by your paired phone for that exact request id. Nomo never sends `permissionOverrides`, `overwrite` or a changed tool input. An interrupt flag makes it answer `deny` ("Stopped from phone"). - **Your `permissions` rules come first** (`settings.json` in that conversation's Antigravity data dir; both CLI and desktop dirs when unclear; read-only), in Antigravity's order Deny > Ask > Allow. Deny and ask rules are read **loosely**: a command rule matches when its command appears anywhere as something that runs — after `sudo`/`env`/`xargs`/`timeout`/`watch`/`stdbuf`/`nice`/`nohup`, inside `sh -c`/`bash -c`/`zsh -c` or `eval`, after `find -exec`, `then` or `!`, as `/bin/rm`, quoted, behind `FOO=1`, after `;`/`&&`/`|`, or inside `$(…)`; a `regex:` rule that does not compile matches everything. A call a deny rule may match never reaches the phone, and a phone Allow can never override it. File paths are normalized (`..`, `.`, repeated `/`) first. Allow rules are read **strictly**: only a single plain command (no separators, subshells, quotes or line breaks) whose words start with the rule's passes straight through, and never a write into Nomo's checkout or state folder. - **One sandbox-retry exception:** after a phone Allow on a shell command, the next call in the same conversation and workspace within 90 s whose arguments are identical except `BypassSandbox`, the one-line summary and the async wait time (the desktop app's retry outside its sandbox) is answered `auto_approve` once, without a new card. Any other difference gets a fresh card; never after a Deny; the one-use ticket is a `0600` file in the sessions folder. - **Own commands:** so that `/nomo-status` doesn't put a card on your phone, the approval hook answers `auto_approve` — on a paired computer, after the deny rules and a pending Stop — for exactly four command lines rebuilt in code from the template the installer writes the skills from (never read from the skill files): status (plain and verbose), approvals status and approvals **on**. Byte-for-byte match (one trailing newline forgiven; a second line, a `cd`, `&& …` or other quoting goes to the phone). Approvals **off**, pair, the pair wait, reset, unpair and the typed pairing code still ask your phone: on a paired computer, pairing again first revokes the current pairing. - **What it reads.** The approval hook: tool name, `CommandLine` or file path, and the model's `toolSummary` (sent sealed). Status events: only `conversationId`, the first `workspacePaths` entry, `transcriptPath` (its mtime and first line) and `modelName` — never tool arguments. From `conversation_summaries.db`: only `title`, `status` and `last_modified_time` of that conversation, read-only; the id must be UUID-shaped before it enters the query, and only the two Antigravity data dirs are read. - **Installer.** Owns exactly the `"nomo"` block in `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (rewritten whole; other blocks untouched; file created as `{}` if absent; refuses a file that is not a JSON object; writes through a symlink). Each registered command first checks its script exists and otherwise answers on its own (`{}`, or `{"decision":"allow"}` for `PreToolUse`), so a moved or deleted `~/.nomo` never blocks a tool. The plugin folder carries a marker file; an unmarked `nomo` folder is someone else's and the installer refuses. The `/nomo-*` skills run only Nomo's own local commands and never print the pairing link or QR secret. Uninstall deletes only that block and the marked folder. ### Devin hooks - **The status hook observes only, except to end a turn you interrupted.** It prints nothing — except that after you tap **Interrupt**, its next `PostToolUse` prints `{"continue":false,"stopReason":"Interrupted from Nomo"}` (the watchdog writes the flag only for an interrupt sealed by your paired phone; the next prompt clears it). From each event it reads only `session_id`, `prompt_id`, the event and tool names, the first prompt (for the title) and `DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR`; from Devin's `sessions.db` only that session's `title`, `model` and `working_directory`, read-only (the id must be a plain slug before it enters the query). - **The approval hook can only defer, approve what you approved, deny what you denied, or pass on your answer.** On `PermissionRequest` it sends the tool name and command or file path sealed, and prints `{"decision":"approve"}` only for an Allow sealed by your paired phone for that exact request id (`{"decision":"block"}` with your note, or "Denied from phone", for a Deny). On `PreToolUse` it holds only `ask_user_question`: questions and options go sealed to the phone, and your answer comes back as `{"decision":"block","reason":"The user answered from their phone (Nomo): …"}` — Devin has no way to take an answer from a hook, so the model reads the decline reason as your answer and the transcript shows the question as rejected. A Deny is a block saying you chose not to answer. **Fail-open:** unpaired, approvals paused, session not on the phone, offline, expiry, crash or timeout all print nothing, leaving Devin's own prompt. If Devin stops waiting (its timeout, Ctrl-C, session end), the hook notices its parent shell is gone, withdraws the card and exits. - **"Always allow (this session)"** is stored only on this computer in `~/.config/cc-status/sessions/.devin-allow` and forgotten when the session ends (or Nomo retires its quiet row), and every one is deleted by unpair, by reset, and when you pair again. While it exists, and only while this computer is paired, a matching request in that session is approved at once, even with approvals paused. A shell grant covers the command's name only for a short list of tools whose arguments cannot run code (`ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `wc`, `touch`, `mkdir`, `grep`, `echo`, `pwd`, `which`, `file`, `stat`, `du`, `cut`, `tr`, `jq`), typed as the bare name, with no shell operators, no glob (`*`, `?`, `[`) and no Devin Desktop `workdir` (`touch` covers `touch b.txt`, not `touchy` or `./touch`). Such a grant still lets `cat`, `grep` or `jq` read any file you can read. Every other command — shells, interpreters, `git`, `make`, `rg`, build tools, agents, `cp`, `rm`, anything with `&&`, `;`, `|`, `$(…)`, backticks or a redirect — is covered only by a grant for that exact text: `git status` does not cover `git -c core.fsmonitor=… status`, and `touch x && rm -rf ~` still asks. An exact grant re-runs that text as-is, in any folder, and does not pin what it runs (`make test` runs whatever the Makefile says then). A shell grant never matches a request carrying any key besides the command and `workdir`. Nomo's own pair, unpair, reset, disable and uninstall commands, and commands whose text or `workdir` names its state folders (`~/.config/cc-status`, `~/.nomo`), are never approved by a grant; quoting tricks are normalized, but a glob can still slip past that check in an exact grant's text (a glob never gets or uses a name grant). For any other tool it covers that tool for the session. - **Own commands:** on a paired computer, before any card, Nomo auto-approves exactly three command lines, rebuilt in code and matched byte for byte against what the skills run (the plugin's `/nomo:*` and the installer's `/nomo-*` forms, with at most Devin Desktop's `workdir` beside them): status, approvals status and approvals **on**. One trailing newline is forgiven; any other difference (`&& …`, `;`, `|`, a redirect, a second line, another script or path, an extra argument) goes to the phone. Approvals **off**, pair, the pair wait, reset, unpair and the typed pairing code still ask your phone: on a paired computer, pairing again first revokes the current pairing. - **Writes.** Devin's own config files are never written by the hooks. The installer writes only its entries in the `"hooks"` key and the marked `nomo-*` skills (which run only Nomo's local commands and never print the pairing link or QR secret); a same-named skill of yours is left alone. A `config.json` with comments is first copied to `config.json.nomo-backup`, then written back without them. The plugin registers the same two bundles through its `hooks.json`, adds no rules, MCP servers or agents, and declares `"platforms": ["local"]`; while the installer's entries are present its copies exit without sending anything. Uninstall removes only Nomo's entries and marked skills. - Devin Desktop's **Restricted Mode** turns hooks off, and Nomo with them. ### Runtime and launch - **Your project's runtime config is never loaded.** Hooks run with your project as working folder, and bun reads `bunfig.toml` (whose `preload` runs code) and `.env` from there. Whenever the runtime is bun, Nomo starts it with `--config=/dev/null --env-file=/dev/null`, including for processes it starts itself (the watchdog). Node reads neither and is started as-is. The working folder is left alone, so version managers (asdf, mise, proto, nodenv) keep working. - **Only installed copies run.** The version-stable hook shim runs the copy that last ran, or the newest installed copy in the Claude Code / Codex plugin cache — never code from a marketplace you added but did not install. - **Runtime floor.** bun before 1.4.4 and Node.js 22 before 22.23.4 are affected by CVE-2026-111497 (brotli decompression). The status commands and the `nomo-ai` installer print a warning naming the runtime and how to upgrade; hooks keep running. - **LAN listener.** Plain HTTP on the local network; the `K_lan` seal is the security boundary. Every rejection is an empty `400` so a prober cannot tell wrong key from stale timestamp from "no pairing here"; requests carry a timestamp and nonce, body size is capped, and commands are still validated (allow-list, freshness, replay dedupe) exactly as on the relay path. ## How it works Every integration runs from one shared `plugin/` directory: a **Claude Code plugin** (`nomo-cc`), a **native Codex plugin** (`nomo`), an **OpenCode plugin module**, and hooks merged into **Cursor**, **Antigravity** and **Devin** config (Devin can also use a native plugin). The hooks, watchdog and commands are single-file `.mjs` bundles that run under **bun or node ≥ 18** (`run.sh` picks whichever is installed); OpenCode loads one resident `.js` bundle. **Zero npm dependencies.** - **Pairing.** `pair` writes a themed local page with a QR and one-time code, derives the key as in [Architecture](#architecture), and writes `~/.config/cc-status/config.json` (`0600`). Every agent reads that same file, so one pairing covers them all and an unpaired hook is a no-op. - **Hook.** Each lifecycle event plans a v2 op (`start` / `update` / `done` / `end` with a `working` / `needsAttention` / `done` status), seals the payload, and POSTs it to the relay, which pushes via APNs. A POST the 2 s timeout cuts off marks the record `updatePending`. - **Liveness watchdog.** Closing a terminal kills the agent with no end event. Each event records `sessions/.json` with the agent's pid; one detached `cc-watchdog.mjs` polls every 5 s and POSTs a corrective `end` once that pid is dead (Codex interrupts are read from the rollout transcript). It re-sends `updatePending` records with a 5 s timeout, backing off 5 s → 60 s after a failure and holding back while an approval hold is live. With no sessions it lingers, while paired, up to 30 min (`IDLE_GRACE_MS`), and the next hook re-spawns it. - **LAN fast path.** When the phone is on the same network, the watchdog hosts a small HTTP listener so commands and answers arrive in <200 ms instead of riding the next relay response (~5–12 s). It is strictly additive: the relay leg runs in parallel and stays canonical, so any LAN failure means "the relay wins", never a lost command. Off by default; turned on in the app. State lives under `~/.config/cc-status/`. `NOMO_WORKER_URL` at pair time points at a staging Worker. ### Claude Code integration Hooks: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Notification`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, `StopFailure`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Elicitation`, `ElicitationResult` — wired by the plugin. Claude Code auto-updates third-party marketplaces only when their `autoUpdate` flag is on (off by default), so `claude plugin update nomo-cc@nomo` is what moves an install. ### Codex integration Codex **≥ 0.142** native plugin `nomo`, sharing `plugin/` with the Claude manifest. Hooks: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `Interrupt`. Its blob is tagged `agent: "codex"` inside the seal. `request_user_input` questions need the Codex task and the Nomo watchdog to share one app-server process. Codex has no plugin update verb: with a `local` marketplace (`source_type` in `~/.codex/config.toml`, the common case) Codex reads the plugin live from the path; with `git`, `codex plugin marketplace upgrade ` refreshes the snapshot. ### OpenCode integration - No marketplace, no hooks: OpenCode auto-discovers `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}`, so `opencode-install.sh` writes `~/.config/opencode/plugins/nomo.js` — a one-line stub **re-exporting** `/plugin/dist/opencode.js` (so the bundle executes beside its sibling `cc-watchdog.mjs`) — and the six `commands/nomo-*.md` with the plugin path baked in. `--project` targets `./.opencode/`. - Deliberately **no npm-resolved plugin**: OpenCode's `Npm.add` short-circuits on an existing cache directory, so a package spec resolves `@latest` once and never updates. The **checkout is the version**, which is why the installer needs a durable `~/.nomo` clone rather than a `bunx` cache. - `/nomo-update` reads its checkout back out of the stub, fetches, reads the target version with `git show :plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (nothing checked out), and only if behind fast-forwards and re-runs the installer. It refuses on a `--ref` pin (detached), a dirty tree, no upstream, diverged history, unreachable remote, or a moved stub. - Plugins are imported once at server start (no hot reload), and the plugin reads the pairing then — so pairing from inside OpenCode needs a restart. The blob is tagged `agent: "opencode"`. Todo lists ride along as plan detail. "Open on Mac" works for the desktop app only (`opencodeLocateTuiPid` walks the server's ancestry for `/OpenCode.app/Contents/MacOS/`). Auto vs. manual approval mode is TUI state that never crosses HTTP, so it is not shown. With `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLAN_MODE` off a plan turn shows only "Planning"; with it on, `plan_exit` arrives as a normal question. Liveness is the OpenCode server process. `opencode --pure` starts without external plugins. - **2.x:** events come from `ctx.event.subscribe` and are translated into the 1.x shapes the plugin already handles (`src/opencode/v2.ts`), so the phone sees the same records either way. The stream is server-wide, so events for other folders are dropped. By default 2.x runs plugins in its background service, not the TUI, so the row's liveness is that service: closing the TUI leaves a finished row, ended when the service stops. A row waiting on a question or a permission the phone cannot answer is closed (`end`, no "finished" alert) about 10–20 s after the last OpenCode window detaches from that service (or from a plain `opencode serve`): the plugin counts the connections into the server's own listening port (`lsof`), since 2.x has no client-presence event. OpenCode keeps the prompt pending; answer it in a reopened window and the row comes back. An Allow/Deny card on the phone is never closed this way, and a running turn is left alone. A background subagent can still be running after the parent's turn shows done; the done frame counts them (`bgAgents`). Other 2.x states ride sealed too: a retry's next attempt time and whether it is rate limiting (`retryAt`, `retryReason`), compaction (`phase`), and a failed or interrupted turn (`outcome`); see [docs/opencode-2x-remote-contract.md](docs/opencode-2x-remote-contract.md). 2.x only produces todos when its `todo` flag is on (`OPENCODE_FLAGS=todo` or `experimental.todo: true`). ### Cursor integration - One user-level `hooks.json` serves both the desktop app and `cursor-agent`. Events: `sessionStart`, `beforeSubmitPrompt`, `postToolUse`, `postToolUseFailure`, `afterShellExecution`, `afterFileEdit`, `stop`, `sessionEnd`. Commands are Cursor skills (`~/.cursor/skills/nomo-*/SKILL.md`). - Status-only: no hold, no answer, and no `locateTuiPid` seam, so a session is only *working* or *done*. - A row starts at `beforeSubmitPrompt`, and only a new prompt reopens a stopped turn. - The title is Cursor's own chat name, one field read read-only with the system `sqlite3` from the desktop app's state database; until then, and for `cursor-agent` chats, the first prompt. - A turn with no `stop` is marked done after 30 quiet minutes; a finished row retires after a little over an hour and returns to working on new activity. - Updating is a `git pull --ff-only` of `~/.nomo` plus a re-run of `cursor-install.mjs`. ### Antigravity integration - `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` serves both the desktop app and the `agy` CLI. Status events `SessionStart`, `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation`, `Stop`, `PostToolUse` run `antigravity-hook.sh ` (10 s timeout); `PreToolUse` runs `antigravity-approve.sh` (24 h). The plugin in `~/.gemini/config/plugins/nomo` carries only skills — plugin-packaged hooks reach only the CLI. An imported `nomo-cc` would report every session twice; the installer says so but never removes it. - A row starts at `PreInvocation`. `PreInvocation`, `PostInvocation` and `PostToolUse` keep it working (throttled); `Stop` marks it done. A turn that ends with no event is settled by the watchdog once the hook's parent process is gone and Antigravity's conversation index shows the run idle after the last event; the 30-minute reap is the last resort. - **Interrupt** stamps a one-shot flag for that conversation (needs the local link); the next `PostInvocation` ends the turn after the current model call or tool. Flags unused within an hour, or left when the turn ended on its own, are dropped; Antigravity's flags are separate from Claude Code's. - **Reply** (up to 4,000 characters, sealed, over LAN and relay) is queued per conversation and handed over at the next `PreInvocation`; a message arriving during the last step makes that turn's `Stop` continue once. The phone shows *Queued* then *Delivered* and can cancel until then. A finished, exited `agy` conversation is resumed with `agy --conversation --print=…`; an `agy` still open keeps the message for your next turn; a finished desktop conversation continues only on the Mac. An Interrupt always wins. - Approval outcomes: Allow → `auto_approve`; Deny → `deny` with your note; everything else → `allow` ("no opinion"). "Always allow" is not offered. If Antigravity cancels the hook mid-hold, the card is withdrawn within seconds and the row returns to working. - The title is `title` from `conversation_summaries.db` in `~/.gemini/antigravity` (desktop) or `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` (`agy`), available after the first turn; before that, the first prompt from the transcript, then the workspace folder. The model badge is `modelName`. ### Devin integration - Two install routes for the Devin CLI and Devin Desktop's Devin Local: the installer (hooks merged into `~/.config/devin/config.json`, read by both) or the native plugin (`.devin-plugin/plugin.json`, `"platforms": ["local"]`, never runs in Devin cloud sessions). If both are present the installer's entries win and the plugin stands down ("both installed — plugin idle" in status). - Hooks: status on `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd` (10 s); approval on `PermissionRequest` and `PreToolUse` matched to `^ask_user_question$` (24 h). Commands are skills — `/nomo:*` from the plugin, `/nomo-*` from the installer. - Interrupt (local link) ends the turn after the current step; Devin cannot cut a command or reply off halfway. While the phone holds a prompt, Devin Desktop shows no buttons of its own for it (like Claude Code's terminal). In Desktop's default Code mode Devin asks only for commands, web fetches and writes outside the project. ### Installer (`nomo-ai`) - A **bootstrapper, not a package manager**: it drives each host's own install path and never writes into `~/.claude` or `~/.codex` itself — a second writer racing `claude plugin update` is how two versions end up fighting over one watchdog. The npm package ships only `bin/`, not the plugin bundle. - With no flags and no terminal it refuses rather than guessing; every failure names the step, exit code and the command to run by hand, and the exit status is non-zero if any agent failed. - Updates: OpenCode, Cursor, Antigravity and Devin legs update `~/.nomo` themselves (the checkout is the version). Claude Code and Codex rows only **print** the host command, because install begins with `marketplace add`, which would silently repoint a marketplace you aimed elsewhere (a fork, a local checkout). A Codex `local` marketplace prints nothing, since there is nothing to run. - **Commands** (`pair`, `status`, `reset`, `unpair`) run the INSTALLED plugin's own entry, not code from the npm package: the highest plugin version among every installed copy — the copy named in the hook shim's stamp (`~/.config/cc-status`), `~/.nomo`, and each version in the Claude Code / Codex plugin caches (the same copies the hook shim considers; superseded Codex copies are skipped) — through that copy's `run.sh`, so the runtime rules in [Runtime and launch](#runtime-and-launch) apply. Nothing installed → one line saying to run `bunx nomo-ai` first. Output and exit status are the entry's own. An unknown word is refused, never treated as an install. - **Short command.** Installed without asking once Nomo is installed (also under `-y`), skipped with `--no-global`, and not reinstalled when this version is already on PATH. It runs exactly `bun add -g nomo-ai` or `npm install -g nomo-ai` (shown first; `-n` only shows it), never with `sudo`, and a failure never changes the exit status. A `nomo` already on PATH counts as this package only if it resolves to `bin/nomo-ai.mjs` beside a `package.json` named `nomo-ai`; any other `nomo` is left alone and never run. The outcome goes to `~/.config/cc-status/short-command`, which the plugin's own output reads (no PATH probe); with no record it names both forms. - `--ref ` applies only to the `~/.nomo` checkout (Claude/Codex marketplaces read the default branch, and the installer says so). The checkout is left **detached** so a later plain run recognises the pin and refuses to fast-forward it. ## Development Sources live in `src/`: `entries/` (bundled entrypoints), `core/` (paths/config, E2E crypto, the hook op planner, agent adapters), `opencode/` (the resident module), `qr/` (vendored QR encoder). All run unmodified under **bun and node ≥ 18** — no `Bun.*` runtime APIs, no npm dependencies. ### Tests ``` bun test ``` Runs the full suite across `core/`, `entries/`, `opencode/` and `qr/`. ### Building the plugin bundle ``` bun build.ts ``` Bundles every hook/command entrypoint in `src/entries/` into `plugin/dist/*.mjs`, inlining local imports so each is one node-runnable file. A second pass bundles `src/opencode/plugin.ts` into `plugin/dist/opencode.js` — **`.js`, not `.mjs`**, because OpenCode's discovery glob is `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}`; it has no `hooks.json` entry and no `hook-shim.sh` row. The OpenCode commands are templates: `plugin/opencode-commands/*.md` (filename = command name) carry a `__NOMO_ROOT__` placeholder that `opencode-install.sh` replaces with the plugin path — OpenCode offers no `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` equivalent. A new `.md` there is picked up with no code change. `plugin/dist/` **is committed.** Marketplace installs are a plain `git clone` with no CI build step, so the committed bundle is what runs. Re-run `bun build.ts` after any source change and commit the result; it was built with `bun 1.3.14` — use the same major/minor to reproduce it byte for byte. ### Releasing The version lives in manifests that must move together (deliberately not repeated here — prose drifts, and `build.ts` checks only the JSON): - `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude Code marketplace) - `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` (Codex marketplace) - `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (`nomo-cc`) - `plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` (`nomo`) - `package.json` (the `nomo-ai` npm bootstrapper) - `.devin-plugin/plugin.json` (the native Devin plugin, `nomo`) OpenCode has no manifest; its checkout is its version. `bun build.ts` refuses to build when the six disagree. `package.json` carries the version only so `bunx nomo-ai --version` is quotable in a bug report.
